How to Make Broasted Chicken: Crunchy Outside, Juicy Inside

Making broasted chicken at home is more than just frying chicken—it’s about mastering a unique cooking method that combines pressure frying with flavorful marinades and coatings. This guide gives you a complete breakdown of everything you need to know: from the broasting technique and step-by-step recipe creation to equipment, variations, and health considerations.

Whether you’re trying to replicate restaurant-style broasted chicken or want to learn healthier alternatives, this in-depth guide covers it all.

Introduction to Broasted Chicken

Broasted chicken is a dish that combines the flavor-packed crispiness of fried chicken with the moisture retention of pressure cooking. Unlike traditional fried chicken, broasting locks in juices while keeping the outside golden and crunchy.

This cooking method was popularized in restaurants but is now a favorite for home cooks worldwide who want the same crispy coating and moist chicken meat without compromising on flavor.

The Broasting Technique Explained

The broasting technique was developed using a pressure fryer, a piece of equipment that combines pressure cooking and deep frying in one. Here’s what makes it special:

  • Pressure Frying: Chicken is cooked under pressure in hot oil, which reduces cooking time and seals in juices.

  • Broasting vs. Frying: While deep frying cooks chicken in open oil, broasting ensures less oil absorption, producing juicier meat with a lighter texture.

  • Pressure Cooking Oil: Used at specific temperatures to achieve that signature crisp while keeping meat tender inside.

Essential Ingredients for Perfect Broasted Chicken

Whole Chicken Pieces

You can use chicken breasts, chicken thighs, chicken drumsticks, or a mix of all for variety.

Marinades and Brines

  • Chicken Marinade: Typically includes buttermilk, lemon juice, soy sauce (optional), hot sauce (for spicier versions), and herbs.

  • Buttermilk Marinade: A classic for tenderizing and flavoring meat.

  • Brine for Chicken: Saltwater brine infused with garlic, thyme, and lemon helps retain moisture.

Flour Coating and Spices

The coating creates the crunch:

  • All-purpose flour and cornstarch for the base.

  • Paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, oregano, thyme, black pepper, salt for seasoning.

  • Double coating enhances crispiness.

Oils and Fats

The right cooking oil is essential:

  • Peanut oil, canola oil, vegetable oil are common.

  • Health-conscious cooks may opt for oils with higher smoke points and healthier fat profiles.

Step-by-Step Recipe Creation

Here’s a complete step-by-step process to create authentic broasted chicken at home.

Step 1: Brining Chicken Before Cooking

  • Mix water, salt, sugar, and herbs like rosemary and thyme.

  • Submerge chicken pieces in the brine for 4–12 hours.

Step 2: Marinating Chicken Overnight

  • Whisk together buttermilk, eggs, hot sauce, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, lemon juice.

  • Add chicken pieces and refrigerate overnight.

Step 3: Preparing the Flour Coating

  • In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, cornstarch, paprika, cayenne pepper, oregano, thyme, and salt.

  • Dredge chicken in flour mixture.

  • Double coating: Dip back into marinade, then dredge again in flour for a thicker, crispy coating.

Step 4: Pressure Frying

  • Preheat pressure fryer with chosen oil to 350°F (175°C).

  • Place coated chicken inside, close lid, and cook under pressure for 8–12 minutes depending on size.

  • Ensure internal temperature reaches 165°F (use a meat thermometer).

Step 5: Draining and Cooling

  • Transfer chicken to a wire rack placed over paper towels.

  • This prevents sogginess and keeps the coating crisp.

Cooking Techniques in Detail

  • Dredging in Flour Mixture: Creates the base layer of crunch.

  • Double Coating for Crispiness: Essential for extra crunch.

  • Draining on Wire Rack: Keeps chicken from getting greasy.

  • Serving with Dips or Sauces: Ranch, garlic mayo, spicy ketchup, or yogurt dips balance flavors.

Recipe Variations

  • Classic Broasted Chicken – Traditional spice mix, perfect for beginners.

  • Spicy Broasted Chicken – Extra cayenne and hot sauce.

  • Herb-Marinated Broasted Chicken – With rosemary, thyme, oregano.

  • Buttermilk Broasted Chicken – Super tender and juicy.

  • Crispy Broasted Chicken Strips – Boneless chicken tenders for kids.

  • Restaurant-Style Broasted Chicken – Mimics popular chains.

  • Broasted Chicken Wings – Great for game nights.

  • Broasted Chicken Sandwiches & Wraps – Served with lettuce, tomato, and sauces.

Related Dishes from Around the World

  • Southern Fried Chicken – American comfort food classic.

  • KFC-Style Chicken – Inspired by fast food flavor profiles.

  • Pakistani Broast Chicken – Street food favorite with spicy marinades.

  • Lebanese Broasted Chicken – Served with garlic sauce and fries.

  • Broasted Chicken Burgers – Crispy fillet inside a bun.

For another delicious oven-based option, check out this baked chicken hindquarters recipe for a crispy, tender twist.

Dietary Adjustments and Healthier Options

  • Low-Sodium Broasted Chicken – Reduce salt in brine.

  • Gluten-Free Coating – Use rice flour or almond flour.

  • Air Fryer Broasted Chicken – Healthier alternative with less oil.

  • Oven-Baked Broasted-Style Chicken – Crispy baked method.

  • Keto Broasted Chicken – Almond flour and pork rind crumbs for coating.

  • Paleo Broasted Chicken – Grain-free flours like cassava or coconut.

Cooking Equipment You’ll Need

  • Broaster Pressure Fryer (ideal for authenticity)

  • Deep Fryer or cast iron skillet as alternatives

  • Heavy-duty pot for stovetop cooking

  • Meat thermometer for doneness

  • Mixing bowls for coatings

  • Wire rack & paper towels for cooling and draining

Health Considerations

  • Calorie Count of Broasted Chicken: Typically lower than deep-fried chicken due to less oil absorption.

  • Fat Content Compared to Fried Chicken: Reduced but still calorie-dense.

  • Healthier Oils for Broasting: Peanut or canola oils are better options.

  • Portion Control: Stick to 2–3 pieces per serving.

  • Balancing with Vegetables or Salads: Lighten the meal with fresh sides.

Popular Recipe Creators & References

Many well-known food platforms and creators share excellent broasted chicken variations:

  • Broaster Company Recipes – Original source of broasting techniques.

  • AllRecipes, Taste of Home, Food Network – Offer home-friendly adaptations.

  • Pakistani & Middle Eastern Food Blogs – Feature spicy street-style broast.

  • YouTube Cooking Channels – Great for step-by-step visuals.

Conclusion

Broasted chicken is more than just fried chicken—it’s a balance of science and flavor. With the right equipment, the perfect chicken marinade, and careful attention to the broasting technique, you can achieve that crispy outside and juicy inside every single time.

From classic recipes to modern, healthier versions, this dish is versatile, flavorful, and universally loved. Try experimenting with marinades, coatings, and cooking methods to make it your own.
